questions.prompt: What is the intent of the Factory Method pattern?

options.text: Define a method for creating an object but let subclasses decide which concrete class to instantiate
Ensure a class has only one instance
Create whole families of related objects at once
Add responsibilities to an object at runtime

questions.explanation: Factory Method defers instantiation of a single product to subclasses. (One instance = Singleton; families = Abstract Factory; runtime responsibilities = Decorator.)

questions.prompt: Which mechanism does Factory Method use to vary which product is created?

options.text: Inheritance — a subclass overrides the factory method
Composition — you hold a separate factory object
Reflection over class names
Cloning an existing instance

questions.explanation: A concrete creator subclass overrides the factory method to return its product. (Composition is how Abstract Factory varies products; cloning is Prototype.)

questions.prompt: In Factory Method, the higher-level code should depend on the Product ____ rather than a concrete product class.
questions.explanation: Returning and using the Product interface keeps the creator decoupled from concrete products.

questions.prompt: Which are genuine benefits of Factory Method? Select all that apply.

options.text: It decouples the code that uses a product from the code that creates it
Adding a new product can be done by adding a subclass, without editing existing code (OCP)
It guarantees only one product instance ever exists
It centralizes creation logic in one method

questions.explanation: Factory Method decouples use from creation, supports OCP, and centralizes creation. Guaranteeing a single instance is Singleton, not Factory Method.

questions.prompt: In TypeScript, what is a common lighter-weight alternative to a Factory Method subclass?

options.text: Passing a factory function that returns the product
Using a global variable
Deep-cloning the creator
Making every field public

questions.explanation: Because functions are first-class in TS, a factory function can carry the creation decision without defining a new subclass.

questions.prompt: What is the main downside of Factory Method?

options.text: It can multiply subclasses, sometimes just to change one product
It makes objects impossible to test
It requires a database
It always slows programs down

questions.explanation: You may create a whole subclass to vary one product, which is overkill when a parameter or factory function would do.
